title: Monetary Regimes and Trade before the Classical Gold Standard: Evidence from the Latin Monetary Union
abstract: arXiv:2510.25487v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: This paper reexamines the trade effects of the Latin Monetary Union (LMU), a 19th century agreement to standardize gold and silver coinage among several European countries. The LMU provides a useful setting for studying whether monetary arrangements fostered trade before the classical gold standard, when gold, silver, bimetallic, and paper regimes coexisted. Because some countries already shared other monetary standards, treating all non-member pairs as a single control group mixes pairs with and without alternative forms of monetary coordination. I classify pairs by standard and estimate the LMU effect relative to pairs without a common standard, bringing the comparison closer to those used in the literature on the gold standard and contemporary currency unions. translated_title: 货币制度与古典金本位之前的贸易：来自拉丁货币联盟的证据
translated_abstract: 本文重新考察了拉丁货币联盟（LMU）的贸易效应。拉丁货币联盟是19世纪多个欧洲国家之间统一金银铸币标准的协定。在古典金本位之前，金本位、银本位、金银复本位和纸币制度并存，而LMU为研究当时的货币安排是否促进贸易提供了有用的研究场景。由于部分国家之间已经共享其他货币标准，若将所有非成员国配对视为单一对照组，就会混淆存在与不存在其他形式货币协调的配对。本文按货币标准对国家配对进行分类，并以没有共同标准的配对作为参照来估计LMU的效应，使比较方式更接近金本位和当代货币联盟文献中所用的方法。结果表明，在复本位制仍然可信的早期阶段，LMU使其成员国之间的贸易增加了约30%。这些效应随后……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文通过按货币标准分类国家配对的改进方法，发现拉丁货币联盟在早期复本位制仍然可信的时期使成员国之间的贸易增加了约30%。
en_tdlr: By classifying country pairs according to their monetary standards, this paper finds that the Latin Monetary Union increased trade among its members by approximately 30% during its early years when bimetallism was still credible.
